Key extracted evidence by paper/stratum (abridged; see attached data collection file for full quotes and locations):

1e482c3c3a (LEAP open tibia):
- Smoking groups: “Patients with unilateral open tibia fractures were divided into 3 baseline smoking categories: never smoked (n = 81), previous smoker (n = 82), and current smoker (n = 105).” (Abstract)
- Infection definitions: “Wound infection was defined as a soft-tissue infection not involving the bone and treated with local debridement and short-term antibiotics.”; “Osteomyelitis was defined as an infection involving the bone and treated with bone debridement and long-term antibiotics.” (Outcome Measures)
- Percent infections by group (Table 2, paraphrased in extraction): never smoked 14.8% infections and 4.9% osteomyelitis; current smokers 24.8% infections and 17.1% osteomyelitis. With denominators 81 and 105 this implies ≈12 vs 26 superficial and 4 vs 18 deep infections.
- Adjusted OR: “Current smoker 2.22 (4.91–1.01)” in “Logistic Regression Analysis: Likelihood of Developing Infection or Osteomyelitis After Adjustment for Patient, Treatment, and Injury Characteristics” (Table 4).

920dc3d62b (adult open tibial shaft fractures):
- Cohort: “Consecutive adult (age >18 years) blunt trauma patients with open tibia shaft fractures (Orthopedic Trauma Association code 42A, B, and C) were included in this observational study.”
- Deep infection definition: “Deep infection was defined as present only if the infection required surgical debridement and long-term IV antibiotics based on infectious disease service consultation.”
- Smoking distribution among infection groups: Table 1 lists “Smoker | 4 (27)” in the infected group and “Smoker | 19 (26)” in the non-infected group, implying 4 smokers with deep infection and 19 smokers without, for 23 smokers total.
- Overall infection count: “Fifteen patients (17%) developed deep infection during their treatment.” Combined with 4 smokers, this yields 11 nonsmokers with deep infection (15–4).
- Univariate OR: Under “Univariate Logistic Regression on Infection Status” Table 1 shows for “Smoker” an OR of 1.05 (95% CI 0.3–3.7).

f3b3fb9a95 (tibial shaft fractures without severe soft-tissue damage):
- Study population: “The purpose of this prospective clinical cohort study was to observe and analyse isolated lower-leg fractures without severe soft-tissue damage in smokers and nonsmokers.”
- Smoking groups: “Thirty-nine patients had never smoked (G1) and 45 patients were current or previous smokers (G2).”
- Infection counts (Table 4): “Superficial: 3 (3.5%); Nonsmokers: 1 (2.6%); Smokers: 2 (4.3%)” and “Deep: 3 (3.5%); Nonsmokers: 2 (5.1%); Smokers: 1 (2.2%).” These give 2 superficial + 1 deep infections in smokers vs 1 superficial + 2 deep in nonsmokers.

f9f2375ade (open tibial fractures, smokers vs nonsmokers):
- Exposure definition: “Patients smoking ten cigarettes or more per day were considered regular smokers. Patients documented as non-smokers were used as a comparison group.”
- Sample sizes: “Complication rates were compared in 140 smoking and 133 non-smoking patients with open tibial fractures.”
- Infection definitions: “Superficial soft tissue infection was diagnosed when there were positive bacteriological wound cultures and clinical signs of soft tissue infection requiring antibiotic treatment. Deep infection was diagnosed in cases where surgical debridement of infected bone was required for control of infection.”
- Infection counts (Results): “Soft tissue infection of the wound associated with the open fracture complicated 21 (15%) group I fractures and 13 (10%) group II fractures. Deep infection complicated 14 (10%) group I and 14 (11%) group II fractures.” Group I and II correspond to smokers (n=140) and non-smokers (n=133), respectively.

6dfe436834 (hip fractures):
- Smoking groups: “For the 3617 patients about whom data was available with respect to smoking habits, there were 467 patients in the smokers group and 3150 in the non-smokers group.”
- Smoking definition: “We define smokers as patients who admit to use of at least one cigarette daily regularly at the time of admission.”
- Superficial infection counts (Table 3): “Superficial wound infection: 7 (1.5%), 59 (1.9%), p=0.705, 0.6–3.1%, 1.4–2.4%” — first count/percent for smokers and second for non-smokers.
- Deep infection counts (Table 3): “Deep wound infection: 2 (0.4%), 21 (0.6%), p=0.770, Too small, 0.4–1.0%”. Again, first number is smokers, second non-smokers.

9ac67a783a (ankle fractures, 906 patients):
- Cohort description: “A consecutive series of patients, aged 15 years or older, operatively treated as a result of an acute ankle fracture during a 3-year period (March 1998 to February 2001) was identified... a total of 906 patients were included in this study.”
- Smoking classification: “For the purpose of this study, the 906 patients were classified as nonsmokers (n = 721) or smokers (n = 185).” For follow-up analysis: “Smokers (N = 183)” and “Nonsmokers (N = 708)” in Table 2.
- Infection definitions: “superficial wound infections (treated with antibiotics or repeated dressings)” and “deep wound infections (below the deep fascia requiring surgical intervention).”
- Superficial infection by smoking (Table 2): row “Superficial wound complication (2) | 27 | 14.8 | 69 | 9.7 | 0.051” — 27 events among 183 smokers (14.8%) vs 69 events among 708 nonsmokers (9.7%).
- Deep infection by smoking (Table 2): row “Deep wound infection (1) | 9 | 4.9 | 6 | 0.8 | <0.001” — 9 events among smokers vs 6 among nonsmokers.
- Adjusted OR (Table 4): “The multivariable analysis (Table 4) showed that smoking was one of the factors associated with development of a deep postoperative wound infection (OR, 6.0; CI, 2.0–18.7). Logistic regression modelling was used… Associations adjusted for: smoking, primary postoperative x-ray unsatisfactory, secondary surgery resulting from malreduction, trimalleolar fracture, insulin-dependent diabetes, open fracture, diabetes of any type, age, having any comorbidity except diabetes, and sex.”

830bf21cf4 (host class predicting infection after open fracture):
- Fracture cohort: “The records of 174 adult patients sustaining open fractures of long bones were retrospectively reviewed. … Each patient was sorted into Class A, B, or C based on 14 immune system compromising factors.”
- Anatomical distribution (Table 2): “Upper arm – 11 (7%), Forearm – 40 (25%), Thigh – 34 (21%), Leg – 77 (48%).”
- Gustilo distribution (Table 2): “Gustilo classification: I — 44 (27%), II — 67 (41%), IIIA — 22 (14%), IIIB — 24 (15%), IIIC — 5 (3%).”
- Infection definition: “Infection was defined as fever, erythema, wound drainage, abscess, or cellulitis, requiring operative treatment.”
- Infection incidence by host class (percentages only): “The incidence of infection was 4%, 15%, and 30% in patients in Classes A, B, and C, respectively.”
- Effect estimate: “One level increase in host class: OR = 2.86, 95% CI: 1.33–6.18, p = 0.007.” (Table 4) in a multiple GEE model.

3b3475937c (geriatric unstable ankle fractures):
- Population: “Ninety-two consecutive patients, 80 females and 12 males, above 80 years of age had open reduction and internal fixation for unstable ankle fractures during the period of January 1998 to August 2007.”
- Fracture openness: “Ninety patients had a closed injury and 2 patients had a Grade 1 open wound.”
- Superficial infection definition and frequency: “Six patients (7%) developed superficial wound infection or breakdown which was successfully treated with oral or intravenous antibiotics for 1 to 2 weeks.”
- Deep infection definition and frequency: “Deep infection occurred in four cases (4.6%) which were initially treated with intravenous antibiotics. However, all four patients eventually required debridement and removal of hardware after 4 to 6 weeks. The wound gradually healed by secondary intention without the need for any plastic surgical intervention.”
- Smoking comorbidity (Table 2): “Smokers: 10 patients.” The narrative states smoking was a significant risk factor for wound complications, but no table cross-tabulates infection by smoking status.

6d465f919c and 620fb1773e:
- These provide detailed smoking and union/bridging analyses but no extractable postoperative wound infection counts by smoking group from the extracted content.

Taken together, these quotes and table values support the structured counts and effect measures summarized in the main answer. For complete line-by-line provenance (including all locations and derivations), see the attached data collection file.

messages.content: whats next?

Short version:

**What we’ve done**

- Mapped all 16 papers (design, fracture type, smoking, which outcomes they report).
- Rated methodological quality / level of evidence for all key studies.
- Built three outcome datasets:
  - **Nonunion vs union by smoking** (long-bone tibia/femur studies only).
  - **Time to union by smoking** (same long-bone set + alcohol‑abuser study only for healing time).
  - **Superficial / deep infection by smoking** (long-bone + ankle + hip where data exist).

Everything is now structured and ready for quantitative synthesis.

---

**What’s next (in order)**

1. **Primary nonunion meta-analysis**
   - Use the nonunion dataset to compute per‑study risk ratios/odds ratios for smokers vs nonsmokers in:
     - All long‑bone fractures.
     - Then tibia‑only and open‑fracture‑only subsets.
   - Fit random‑effects models, produce forest plots, and summarize heterogeneity.

2. **Infection meta-analyses**
   - Pool superficial infection risks by smoking across:
     - Long‑bone/open‑tibia studies.
     - Ankle and hip series.
   - Repeat for deep infection.

3. **Time‑to‑union meta-analyses**
   - Convert time‑to‑union data to mean differences (weeks) smokers vs nonsmokers.
   - Pool:
     - All long‑bone fractures.
     - Tibia‑only and open‑only subsets.

4. **Sensitivity analyses**
   - Restrict to higher‑LOE / higher‑quality studies.
   - Apply your special rules (e.g., alcohol‑abuser study only in time‑to‑union, host‑classification only in infection‑by‑host, not in smoking‑nonunion).

If you’re fine with that sequence, I’ll start **coding the primary nonunion meta‑analysis** next (all long‑bone fractures, smokers vs nonsmokers) and show you the first pooled estimate + forest plot.
Sounds good!
Working on that now...

messages.content: Now I'll compute effect sizes, restrict to clearly usable strata (dropping rows with missing counts), run a random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian–Laird on log risk ratios), and generate a forest plot for the primary nonunion outcome (any long-bone fractures, smokers vs nonsmokers).

function.arguments:
{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load nonunion data
nonunion_file = load_analyst_data('Nonunion and Union Status Analyst', 'UnionNonunionSmokingOutcomes')
df = pd.read_csv(nonunion_file)

# Keep rows with full 2x2 counts
mask_counts = df['exposed_group_nonunion_count_value'].notna() & df['reference_group_nonunion_count_value'].notna()
non = df[mask_counts].copy()
print('Usable nonunion studies:', len(non))
print(non[['id','paper_title','stratum_label_value','exposed_group_n_at_risk_value','exposed_group_nonunion_count_value','reference_group_n_at_risk_value','reference_group_nonunion_count_value']])

# Calculate risk ratios (RR) with continuity correction if any zero cells
records = []
for i,row in non.iterrows():
    a = row['exposed_group_nonunion_count_value']
    b = row['exposed_group_n_at_risk_value'] - a
    c = row['reference_group_nonunion_count_value']
    d = row['reference_group_n_at_risk_value'] - c

    # continuity correction if any cell zero
    if 0 in [a,b,c,d]:
        cc = 0.5
        a_cc, b_cc, c_cc, d_cc = a+cc, b+cc, c+cc, d+cc
    else:
        a_cc, b_cc, c_cc, d_cc = a,b,c,d
    risk_exposed = a_cc / (a_cc + b_cc)
    risk_ref = c_cc / (c_cc + d_cc)
    rr = risk_exposed / risk_ref
    log_rr = np.log(rr)
    se_log_rr = np.sqrt(1/a_cc - 1/(a_cc + b_cc) + 1/c_cc - 1/(c_cc + d_cc))

    records.append({
        'id': row['id'],
        'paper_title': row['paper_title'],
        'stratum_label_value': row['stratum_label_value'],
        'a': a, 'b': b, 'c': c, 'd': d,
        'rr': rr, 'log_rr': log_rr, 'se_log_rr': se_log_rr
    })

es = pd.DataFrame(records)
print('\nEffect sizes:')
print(es[['id','rr','log_rr','se_log_rr']])

# Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird) on log RR
w_fixed = 1/es['se_log_rr']**2
log_rr_fixed = np.sum(w_fixed*es['log_rr'])/np.sum(w_fixed)
Q = np.sum(w_fixed*(es['log_rr'] - log_rr_fixed)**2)
df_Q = len(es) - 1
C = np.sum(w_fixed) - np.sum(w_fixed**2)/np.sum(w_fixed)
tau2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/C)

w_random = 1/(es['se_log_rr']**2 + tau2)
log_rr_random = np.sum(w_random*es['log_rr'])/np.sum(w_random)
se_log_rr_random = np.sqrt(1/np.sum(w_random))
rr_random = np.exp(log_rr_random)
ci_low = np.exp(log_rr_random - 1.96*se_log_rr_random)
ci_high = np.exp(log_rr_random + 1.96*se_log_rr_random)

print('\nRandom-effects pooled RR (nonunion, all long-bone strata):')
print('RR = {:.2f}, 95% CI {:.2f}–{:.2f}'.format(rr_random, ci_low, ci_high))
print('tau^2 = {:.4f}'.format(tau2))

# Forest plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
y = np.arange(len(es))
ax.errorbar(es['rr'], y, xerr=1.96*es['se_log_rr'].apply(lambda s: np.exp(np.log(es['rr'])+s) - es['rr']), fmt='o', color='black')
# Plot CIs correctly using log scale
ax.clear()

for i, row in es.iterrows():
    rr_i = row['rr']
    se_i = row['se_log_rr']
    log_rr_i = row['log_rr']
    ci_low_i = np.exp(log_rr_i - 1.96*se_i)
    ci_high_i = np.exp(log_rr_i + 1.96*se_i)
    idx = es.index.get_loc(i)
    ax.plot([ci_low_i, ci_high_i], [idx, idx], '-', color='black')
    ax.plot(rr_i, idx, 's', color='black')

# Add pooled
idx_pool = len(es)
ax.plot([ci_low, ci_high], [idx_pool, idx_pool], '-', color='red')
ax.plot(rr_random, idx_pool, 's', color='red')

# y-ticks
labels = list(es['id']) + ['Pooled']
ax.set_yticks(range(len(es)+1))
ax.set_yticklabels(labels)
ax.set_xscale('log')
ax.set_xlabel('Risk Ratio for Nonunion (smokers vs nonsmokers)')
ax.axvline(1, color='grey', linestyle='--')
ax.invert_yaxis()
plt.tight_layout()

plot_file = 'nonunion_forest_overall.png'
plt.savefig(plot_file, dpi=300)
print('Saved forest plot to', plot_file)
"}

{"code":"import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# --- Nonunion: crude OR meta-analysis ---
nonunion_file = load_analyst_data('Nonunion and Union Status Analyst', 'UnionNonunionSmokingOutcomes')
nu_df = pd.read_csv(nonunion_file)

mask_counts = nu_df['exposed_group_nonunion_count_value'].notna() & nu_df['reference_group_nonunion_count_value'].notna()
nu = nu_df[mask_counts].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

records = []
for _, row in nu.iterrows():
    a = row['exposed_group_nonunion_count_value']
    b = row['exposed_group_n_at_risk_value'] - a
    c = row['reference_group_nonunion_count_value']
    d = row['reference_group_n_at_risk_value'] - c
    # continuity correction if any zero cell
    if 0 in [a,b,c,d]:
        cc = 0.5
        a_cc, b_cc, c_cc, d_cc = a+cc, b+cc, c+cc, d+cc
    else:
        a_cc, b_cc, c_cc, d_cc = a,b,c,d
    or_val = (a_cc*d_cc)/(b_cc*c_cc)
    log_or = np.log(or_val)
    se_log_or = np.sqrt(1/a_cc + 1/b_cc + 1/c_cc + 1/d_cc)
    records.append({
        'id': row['id'],
        'paper_title': row['paper_title'],
        'stratum': row['stratum_label_value'],
        'a': a, 'b': b, 'c': c, 'd': d,
        'or': or_val,
        'log_or': log_or,
        'se_log_or': se_log_or
    })

es_nu = pd.DataFrame(records)

# DerSimonian–Laird random-effects on log OR
w_fixed = 1/es_nu['se_log_or']**2
log_or_fixed = np.sum(w_fixed*es_nu['log_or'])/np.sum(w_fixed)
Q = np.sum(w_fixed*(es_nu['log_or'] - log_or_fixed)**2)
df_Q = len(es_nu) - 1
C = np.sum(w_fixed) - np.sum(w_fixed**2)/np.sum(w_fixed)
tau2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/C)

w_random = 1/(es_nu['se_log_or']**2 + tau2)
log_or_random = np.sum(w_random*es_nu['log_or'])/np.sum(w_random)
se_log_or_random = np.sqrt(1/np.sum(w_random))
pooled_or = np.exp(log_or_random)
ci_low = np.exp(log_or_random - 1.96*se_log_or_random)
ci_high = np.exp(log_or_random + 1.96*se_log_or_random)
I2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/Q*100) if Q>0 else 0

print('Nonunion crude OR meta-analysis (all long-bone strata):')
print(es_nu[['id','or','log_or','se_log_or']])
print('\nPooled OR = {:.2f} (95% CI {:.2f}–{:.2f}), tau^2 = {:.4f}, I^2 = {:.1f}%'.format(pooled_or, ci_low, ci_high, tau2, I2))

# Save study-level and pooled results

Here’s the first core result using **crude odds ratios (ORs)**, plus what comes next.

---

## 1. Nonunion: crude OR meta-analysis (all long-bone strata)

Using the 7 strata with full 2×2 data (smokers vs nonsmokers):

Studies included:

- 920dc3d62b – Open tibia fractures (Enninghorst 2011)  
- a154656aa1 – Allograft + DBM nonunion/fracture grafts (Ziran)  
- bc42862567 – Femoral shaft fractures (Taitsman)  
- c0e963edee – Femoral diaphyseal fractures (Giannoudis)  
- f3b3fb9a95 – Tibial shaft fractures (Moghaddam)  
- f7e1801e7a – Distal tibial fractures with hybrid external fixation (Ristiniemi)  
- f9f2375ade – Open tibial fractures (Adams)

For each, I computed a **crude OR** for nonunion:

- a = nonunions in smokers  
- b = unions in smokers  
- c = nonunions in nonsmokers  
- d = unions in nonsmokers  
- OR = (a·d)/(b·c), with a 0.5 continuity correction if any cell is zero.

### Study-level crude ORs

(OR > 1 means higher nonunion odds in smokers):

- 920dc3d62b (open tibia, 12‑mo union): **OR ≈ 2.26**
- a154656aa1 (DBM/allograft grafts): **OR ≈ 5.06**
- bc42862567 (femoral shaft): **OR ≈ 3.25**
- c0e963edee (femoral diaphysis): **OR ≈ 2.29**
- f3b3fb9a95 (tibial shaft): **OR ≈ 20.56** (small N, one cell = 0)
- f7e1801e7a (distal tibia, hybrid EF): **OR ≈ 4.04**
- f9f2375ade (open tibia): **OR ≈ 1.48**

### Pooled result (random-effects, DerSimonian–Laird)

- **Pooled OR for nonunion (smokers vs nonsmokers)**  
  = **2.41 (95% CI 1.62–3.59)**  
- Between‑study heterogeneity:
  - τ² ≈ 0.048  
  - Q ≈ 7.16, df = 6  
  - **I² ≈ 16.7%** (low–moderate heterogeneity)

Interpretation (crude, all long‑bone strata):

> Across these 7 long‑bone/nonunion strata, smokers have roughly **2.4‑fold higher odds of nonunion** compared with nonsmokers, with relatively low between‑study heterogeneity.

The forest plot `forest_nonunion_OR2.png` summarizes these visually (you can download it from the link the system shows).

---

## 2. What’s next with crude ORs

With nonunion done on crude ORs, next steps are:

1. **Crude OR meta-analyses for infection**
   - Use the **Smoking_Infection_Outcomes** dataset to compute crude ORs for:
     - **Deep infection** (smokers vs nonsmokers) across:
       - Open tibia (Adams, Enninghorst, LEAP if usable as 2×2 approximation)
       - Tibial shaft (Moghaddam)  
       - Hip (Smoking & hip fracture)  
       - Ankle (906‑patient ankle series)
     - **Superficial infection** in the same papers where available.
   - Then:
     - Pooled ORs for deep infection.  
     - Pooled ORs for superficial infection.  
     - Forest plots for each.

2. **Crude mean-difference meta-analyses for healing time**
   - Use `TimeToUnionBySmoking`:
     - Convert group means/SDs (or approximate from medians where we decide that’s acceptable) into **mean differences** in weeks, smokers vs nonsmokers.
     - Pooled MDs for:
       - All long‑bones.  
       - Tibia‑only and open‑only where possible.

3. **Sensitivity & subgroup analyses**
   - Restrict nonunion and infection analyses to:
     - Tibia‑only or open‑fracture‑only.  
     - Higher‑LOE / better‑quality studies.
   - Optionally compare crude ORs vs adjusted ORs (e.g., LEAP, ankle deep infection).

Unless you want me to prioritize a different outcome, I will next:

- Run **crude OR meta‑analyses for deep and superficial infections**, and report pooled ORs + forest plots.

function.arguments:
{"code":"import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

inf_file = load_analyst_data('Infection Outcomes by Smoking Analyst', 'Smoking_Infection_Outcomes')
df = pd.read_csv(inf_file)

# Helper to compute crude ORs given a,b,c,d

def compute_or(a,b,c,d):
    # continuity correction
    if 0 in [a,b,c,d]:
        cc=0.5
        a_cc,b_cc,c_cc,d_cc = a+cc,b+cc,c+cc,d+cc
    else:
        a_cc,b_cc,c_cc,d_cc = a,b,c,d
    or_val = (a_cc*d_cc)/(b_cc*c_cc)
    log_or = np.log(or_val)
    se = np.sqrt(1/a_cc + 1/b_cc + 1/c_cc + 1/d_cc)
    return or_val, log_or, se

# Identify rows with raw counts available
print(df[['id','paper_title','raw_counts_available_value']])

usable = df[df['raw_counts_available_value']==True].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
print('\nUsable infection strata with raw counts:')
print(usable[['id','paper_title','stratum_description_value']])

# We'll analyze superficial and deep separately for these rows
super_records = []
deep_records = []

for _,row in usable.iterrows():
    id_ = row['id']
    title = row['paper_title']
    stratum = row['stratum_description_value']
    Ne = row['exposed_group_n_at_risk_value']
    Nr = row['reference_group_n_at_risk_value']
    # superficial
    se = row['exposed_group_superficial_infections_value']
    sr = row['reference_group_superficial_infections_value']
    if not np.isnan(se) and not np.isnan(sr):
        a,b,c,d = se, Ne-se, sr, Nr-sr
        or_val, log_or, se_log = compute_or(a,b,c,d)
        super_records.append({'id':id_,'paper_title':title,'stratum':stratum,
                              'a':a,'b':b,'c':c,'d':d,
                              'or':or_val,'log_or':log_or,'se_log_or':se_log})
    # deep
    de = row['exposed_group_deep_infections_value']
    dr = row['reference_group_deep_infections_value']
    if not np.isnan(de) and not np.isnan(dr):
        a,b,c,d = de, Ne-de, dr, Nr-dr
        or_val, log_or, se_log = compute_or(a,b,c,d)
        deep_records.append({'id':id_,'paper_title':title,'stratum':stratum,
                              'a':a,'b':b,'c':c,'d':d,
                              'or':or_val,'log_or':log_or,'se_log_or':se_log})

super_df = pd.DataFrame(super_records)
deep_df = pd.DataFrame(deep_records)

print('\nSuperficial infection crude OR data:')
print(super_df[['id','or','log_or','se_log_or']])
print('\nDeep infection crude OR data:')
print(deep_df[['id','or','log_or','se_log_or']])

# Meta-analysis function

def meta_random(es):
    w_fixed = 1/es['se_log_or']**2
    log_or_fixed = np.sum(w_fixed*es['log_or'])/np.sum(w_fixed)
    Q = np.sum(w_fixed*(es['log_or'] - log_or_fixed)**2)
    df_Q = len(es)-1
    C = np.sum(w_fixed) - np.sum(w_fixed**2)/np.sum(w_fixed)
    tau2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/C) if len(es)>1 else 0
    w_random = 1/(es['se_log_or']**2 + tau2)
    log_or_random = np.sum(w_random*es['log_or'])/np.sum(w_random)
    se_random = np.sqrt(1/np.sum(w_random))
    pooled_or = np.exp(log_or_random)
    ci_low = np.exp(log_or_random - 1.96*se_random)
    ci_high = np.exp(log_or_random + 1.96*se_random)
    I2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/Q*100) if Q>0 and len(es)>1 else 0
    return pooled_or, ci_low, ci_high, tau2, Q, df_Q, I2

# Run meta-analyses
if len(super_df)>0:
    pooled_or_s, ci_l_s, ci_h_s, tau2_s, Q_s, dfQ_s, I2_s = meta_random(super_df)
    print('\nSuperficial infection pooled OR = {:.2f} (95% CI {:.2f}–{:.2f}), tau^2 = {:.4f}, I^2 = {:.1f}%'.format(pooled_or_s, ci_l_s, ci_h_s, tau2_s, I2_s))

if len(deep_df)>0:
    pooled_or_d, ci_l_d, ci_h_d, tau2_d, Q_d, dfQ_d, I2_d = meta_random(deep_df)
    print('Deep infection pooled OR = {:.2f} (95% CI {:.2f}–{:.2f}), tau^2 = {:.4f}, I^2 = {:.1f}%'.format(pooled_or_d, ci_l_d, ci_h_d, tau2_d, I2_d))

# Save results
super_df['ci_low'] = np.exp(super_df['log_or'] - 1.96*super_df['se_log_or'])
super_df['ci_high'] = np.exp(super_df['log_or'] + 1.96*super_df['se_log_or'])
deep_df['ci_low'] = np.exp(deep_df['log_or'] - 1.96*deep_df['se_log_or'])
deep_df['ci_high'] = np.exp(deep_df['log_or'] + 1.96*deep_df['se_log_or'])

super_df.to_csv('infection_superficial_crude_ORs.csv', index=False)
deep_df.to_csv('infection_deep_crude_ORs.csv', index=False)

meta_inf = []
if len(super_df)>0:
    meta_inf.append({'type':'superficial','pooled_or':pooled_or_s,'ci_low':ci_l_s,'ci_high':ci_h_s,'tau2':tau2_s,'Q':Q_s,'df_Q':dfQ_s,'I2':I2_s})
if len(deep_df)>0:
    meta_inf.append({'type':'deep','pooled_or':pooled_or_d,'ci_low':ci_l_d,'ci_high':ci_h_d,'tau2':tau2_d,'Q':Q_d,'df_Q':dfQ_d,'I2':I2_d})

pd.DataFrame(meta_inf).to_csv('infection_or_meta_results.csv', index=False)

# Forest plots
for label,es in [('superficial', super_df), ('deep', deep_df)]:
    if len(es)==0:
        continue
    pooled_or, ci_l, ci_h, tau2, Q, dfQ, I2 = meta_random(es)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    for i, row in es.iterrows():
        or_i = row['or']
        se_i = row['se_log_or']
        log_or_i = row['log_or']
        ci_l_i = np.exp(log_or_i - 1.96*se_i)
        ci_h_i = np.exp(log_or_i + 1.96*se_i)
        ax.plot([ci_l_i, ci_h_i], [i, i], '-', color='black')
        ax.plot(or_i, i, 's', color='black')
    idx_pool = len(es)
    ax.plot([ci_l, ci_h], [idx_pool, idx_pool], '-', color='red')
    ax.plot(pooled_or, idx_pool, 's', color='red')
    labels = list(es['id']) + ['Pooled']
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(es)+1))
    ax.set_yticklabels(labels)
    ax.set_xscale('log')
    ax.set_xlabel(f'Odds Ratio for {label.capitalize()} Infection (smokers vs nonsmokers)')
    ax.axvline(1, color='grey', linestyle='--')
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    plt.tight_layout()
    fname = f'forest_{label}_infection.png'
    plt.savefig(fname, dpi=300)
    print('Saved', fname)
"}

Here are the crude OR meta-analysis results we’ve now run.

---

## 1. Nonunion (primary outcome) – crude ORs

Studies/strata included (7 long-bone strata with full 2×2 data):

- Open tibia (Enninghorst 2011, 920dc3d62b)  
- Allograft + DBM fractures/nonunions (Ziran, a154656aa1)  
- Femoral shaft fractures (Taitsman, bc42862567)  
- Femoral diaphysis fractures (Giannoudis, c0e963edee)  
- Tibial shaft fractures (Moghaddam, f3b3fb9a95)  
- Distal tibial fractures with hybrid external fixation (Ristiniemi, f7e1801e7a)  
- Open tibial fractures (Adams, f9f2375ade)

Each OR compares **smokers vs nonsmokers**, using crude 2×2 counts (with 0.5 continuity correction where needed).

### Study-level crude ORs for nonunion

- 920dc3d62b (open tibia, 12‑mo union): OR ≈ **2.26**
- a154656aa1 (DBM/allograft): OR ≈ **5.06**
- bc42862567 (femoral shaft): OR ≈ **3.25**
- c0e963edee (femoral diaphysis): OR ≈ **2.29**
- f3b3fb9a95 (tibial shaft): OR ≈ **20.6** (small N; one zero cell; very imprecise)
- f7e1801e7a (distal tibia, hybrid EF): OR ≈ **4.04**
- f9f2375ade (open tibia): OR ≈ **1.48**

### Pooled crude OR (random-effects, DerSimonian–Laird)

- **Pooled OR for nonunion** (smokers vs nonsmokers):  
  **2.41 (95% CI 1.62–3.59)**  
- Between‑study heterogeneity:  
  - τ² ≈ 0.048  
  - I² ≈ **16.7%** (low–moderate)

Interpretation (crude):

> Across these long‑bone strata, **smokers have ~2.4× the odds of nonunion** compared with nonsmokers, even without adjustment for other risk factors.

The file `nonunion_2x2_data.csv` has all per‑study 2×2 and ORs; `forest_nonunion_OR2.png` is the forest plot.

---

## 2. Superficial infection – crude ORs

Strata with raw 2×2 infection data:

- 6dfe436834 – Hip fractures (smokers vs non-smokers)  
- f3b3fb9a95 – Isolated tibial shaft fractures (mixed open/closed, limited soft-tissue damage)  
- f9f2375ade – Open tibial fractures

Each provides **superficial wound infection** counts by smoking group.

### Study-level crude ORs (superficial infection)

- 6dfe436834 (hip): OR ≈ **0.80**  
- f3b3fb9a95 (tibia): OR ≈ **1.77**  
- f9f2375ade (open tibia): OR ≈ **1.63**

### Pooled crude OR (random-effects)

- **Pooled OR for superficial infection**:  
  **1.19 (95% CI 0.70–2.02)**  
- τ² ≈ 0, **I² = 0%** (no detectable heterogeneity)

Interpretation:

> On crude data, smokers may have a modestly higher superficial infection risk, but the CI is wide and includes no effect; the pooled estimate is **not statistically significant**.

`infection_superficial_crude_ORs.csv` has per‑study values; `forest_superficial_infection.png` shows the forest plot.

---

## 3. Deep infection – crude ORs

Strata with deep infection 2×2 data:

- 6dfe436834 – Hip fractures  
- 920dc3d62b – Open tibial shaft fractures (deep infection as defined by debridement + IV antibiotics)  
- f3b3fb9a95 – Tibial shaft fractures (small numbers)  
- f9f2375ade – Open tibial fractures (deep bone infection requiring debridement)

### Study-level crude ORs (deep infection)

- 6dfe436834 (hip): OR ≈ **0.64**  
- 920dc3d62b (open tibia): OR ≈ **1.05**  
- f3b3fb9a95 (tibia): OR ≈ **0.42** (very small n)  
- f9f2375ade (open tibia): OR ≈ **0.94**

### Pooled crude OR (random-effects)

- **Pooled OR for deep infection**:  
  **0.87 (95% CI 0.48–1.56)**  
- τ² ≈ 0, **I² = 0%**

Interpretation:

> With available crude counts, there is **no clear evidence that smokers have higher odds of deep infection**; the point estimate is slightly below 1, but imprecise with wide CI crossing 1.

`infection_deep_crude_ORs.csv` has per‑study 2×2 and ORs; `forest_deep_infection.png` shows the forest plot.

---

## 4. Where this leaves us

Using **crude** analyses:

- **Nonunion**: strong and consistent signal – ~2.4× higher odds in smokers.  
- **Superficial infection**: trend toward higher risk but not significant; CI compatible with substantial harm or no effect.  
- **Deep infection**: no overall increased risk observed in crude data.

Next steps (if you’d like to continue):

1. **Time‑to‑union meta-analysis**  
   - Use the `TimeToUnionBySmoking` dataset to compute pooled mean differences in healing time (weeks) smokers vs nonsmokers, with tibia‑only and open‑only subsets.

2. **Sensitivity analyses**  
   - Restrict nonunion and infection analyses to:
     - Tibial fractures only.  
     - Open fractures only.  
     - Higher‑quality / higher‑LOE studies.  
   - Optionally compare crude vs adjusted ORs (e.g., LEAP, ankle deep infection).

- Move on to **time‑to‑union pooling next**,  
- Or dig into **subgroup/sensitivity** on any of the crude OR results we just generated.

{"code":"import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fname = load_analyst_data('Time-to-Union Outcome Analyst', 'TimeToUnionBySmoking')
tt = pd.read_csv(fname)

# Identify rows with usable mean+variance info
mask_mean = tt['exposed_group_time_to_union_mean_value'].notna() & tt['reference_group_time_to_union_mean_value'].notna()
mask_var = (
    tt['exposed_group_time_to_union_sd_value'].notna() & tt['reference_group_time_to_union_sd_value'].notna()
) | (
    tt['exposed_group_time_to_union_se_value'].notna() & tt['reference_group_time_to_union_se_value'].notna()
)
use = tt[mask_mean & mask_var].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
print('Usable time-to-union strata:', len(use))
print(use[['id','paper_title','fracture_site_value','fracture_type_value','subgroup_descriptor_value','time_unit_value',
           'exposed_group_label_value','reference_group_label_value','exposed_group_n_value','reference_group_n_value',
           'exposed_group_time_to_union_mean_value','reference_group_time_to_union_mean_value',
           'exposed_group_time_to_union_sd_value','reference_group_time_to_union_sd_value',
           'exposed_group_time_to_union_se_value','reference_group_time_to_union_se_value']])

# Convert to weeks and SDs
records = []
for _,row in use.iterrows():
    id_ = row['id']
    title = row['paper_title']
    site = row['fracture_site_value']
    frac_type = row['fracture_type_value']
    subgroup = row['subgroup_descriptor_value']
    unit = row['time_unit_value']
    N1 = row['exposed_group_n_value']
    N0 = row['reference_group_n_value']
    m1 = row['exposed_group_time_to_union_mean_value']
    m0 = row['reference_group_time_to_union_mean_value']
    sd1 = row['exposed_group_time_to_union_sd_value']
    sd0 = row['reference_group_time_to_union_sd_value']
    se1 = row['exposed_group_time_to_union_se_value']
    se0 = row['reference_group_time_to_union_se_value']

    # determine SD
    if not np.isnan(sd1) and not np.isnan(sd0):
        SD1, SD0 = sd1, sd0
    elif not np.isnan(se1) and not np.isnan(se0):
        SD1 = se1 * np.sqrt(N1)
        SD0 = se0 * np.sqrt(N0)
    else:
        continue

    # convert units to weeks
    if unit == 'weeks':
        m1_w, m0_w = m1, m0
        SD1_w, SD0_w = SD1, SD0
    elif unit == 'days':
        m1_w, m0_w = m1/7.0, m0/7.0
        SD1_w, SD0_w = SD1/7.0, SD0/7.0
    elif unit == 'months':
        # assume 4.345 weeks/month (approx)
        factor = 4.345
        m1_w, m0_w = m1*factor, m0*factor
        SD1_w, SD0_w = SD1*factor, SD0*factor
    else:
        # unknown units; skip
        continue

    md = m1_w - m0_w  # smokers - nonsmokers
    se_md = np.sqrt(SD1_w**2/N1 + SD0_w**2/N0)
    records.append({
        'id': id_, 'paper_title': title, 'fracture_site_value': site, 'fracture_type_value': frac_type,
        'subgroup_descriptor_value': subgroup,
        'N_smokers': N1, 'N_nonsmokers': N0,
        'mean_weeks_smokers': m1_w, 'mean_weeks_nonsmokers': m0_w,
        'sd_weeks_smokers': SD1_w, 'sd_weeks_nonsmokers': SD0_w,
        'md_weeks': md, 'se_md': se_md
    })

es = pd.DataFrame(records)
print('\nEffect-size dataset (time-to-union MDs):')
print(es)

# Random-effects meta-analysis on MD
if len(es) > 0:
    w_fixed = 1/es['se_md']**2
    md_fixed = np.sum(w_fixed*es['md_weeks'])/np.sum(w_fixed)
    Q = np.sum(w_fixed*(es['md_weeks'] - md_fixed)**2)
    df_Q = len(es) - 1
    C = np.sum(w_fixed) - np.sum(w_fixed**2)/np.sum(w_fixed)
    tau2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/C) if len(es) > 1 else 0
    w_random = 1/(es['se_md']**2 + tau2)
    md_random = np.sum(w_random*es['md_weeks'])/np.sum(w_random)
    se_random = np.sqrt(1/np.sum(w_random))
    ci_low = md_random - 1.96*se_random
    ci_high = md_random + 1.96*se_random
    I2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/Q*100) if Q>0 and len(es)>1 else 0

    print('\nRandom-effects pooled mean difference (smokers - nonsmokers, weeks):')
    print('MD = {:.2f} weeks (95% CI {:.2f to} {:.2f}), tau^2 = {:.4f}, I^2 = {:.1f}%'.format(md_random, ci_low, ci_high, tau2, I2))

    # Save data
    es.to_csv('healing_time_differences_descriptive.csv', index=False)

    # Simple bar plot of MDs
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4))
    y = np.arange(len(es))
    ax.errorbar(es['md_weeks'], y, xerr=1.96*es['se_md'], fmt='s', color='black')
    ax.axvline(0, color='grey', linestyle='--')
    ax.set_yticks(y)
    ax.set_yticklabels(es['id'])
    ax.set_xlabel('Mean difference in healing time (weeks), smokers - nonsmokers')
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    plt.tight_layout()
    fname = 'healing_time_diff_bar.png'
    plt.savefig(fname, dpi=300)
    print('Saved', fname)
"}

{"code":"import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fname = load_analyst_data('Time-to-Union Outcome Analyst', 'TimeToUnionBySmoking')

mask_mean = tt['exposed_group_time_to_union_mean_value'].notna() & tt['reference_group_time_to_union_mean_value'].notna()
mask_var = (
    tt['exposed_group_time_to_union_sd_value'].notna() & tt['reference_group_time_to_union_sd_value'].notna()
) | (
    tt['exposed_group_time_to_union_se_value'].notna() & tt['reference_group_time_to_union_se_value'].notna()
)
use = tt[mask_mean & mask_var].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

records = []
for _,row in use.iterrows():
    id_ = row['id']
    title = row['paper_title']
    unit = row['time_unit_value']
    N1 = row['exposed_group_n_value']
    N0 = row['reference_group_n_value']
    m1 = row['exposed_group_time_to_union_mean_value']
    m0 = row['reference_group_time_to_union_mean_value']
    sd1 = row['exposed_group_time_to_union_sd_value']
    sd0 = row['reference_group_time_to_union_sd_value']
    se1 = row['exposed_group_time_to_union_se_value']
    se0 = row['reference_group_time_to_union_se_value']

    if not np.isnan(sd1) and not np.isnan(sd0):
        SD1, SD0 = sd1, sd0
    elif not np.isnan(se1) and not np.isnan(se0):
        SD1 = se1 * np.sqrt(N1)
        SD0 = se0 * np.sqrt(N0)
    else:
        continue

    # convert units to weeks
    if unit == 'weeks':
        m1_w, m0_w = m1, m0
        SD1_w, SD0_w = SD1, SD0
    elif unit == 'days':
        m1_w, m0_w = m1/7.0, m0/7.0
        SD1_w, SD0_w = SD1/7.0, SD0/7.0
    elif unit == 'months':
        factor = 4.345
        m1_w, m0_w = m1*factor, m0*factor
        SD1_w, SD0_w = SD1*factor, SD0*factor
    else:
        continue

    md = m1_w - m0_w
    se_md = np.sqrt(SD1_w**2/N1 + SD0_w**2/N0)
    records.append({
        'id': id_, 'paper_title': title,
        'N_smokers': N1, 'N_nonsmokers': N0,
        'mean_weeks_smokers': m1_w, 'mean_weeks_nonsmokers': m0_w,
        'sd_weeks_smokers': SD1_w, 'sd_weeks_nonsmokers': SD0_w,
        'md_weeks': md, 'se_md': se_md
    })

es = pd.DataFrame(records)
print('Usable strata for time-to-union MD:', len(es))
print(es)

if len(es) > 0:
    w_fixed = 1/es['se_md']**2
    md_fixed = np.sum(w_fixed*es['md_weeks'])/np.sum(w_fixed)
    Q = np.sum(w_fixed*(es['md_weeks'] - md_fixed)**2)
    df_Q = len(es) - 1
    C = np.sum(w_fixed) - np.sum(w_fixed**2)/np.sum(w_fixed)
    tau2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/C) if len(es) > 1 else 0
    w_random = 1/(es['se_md']**2 + tau2)
    md_random = np.sum(w_random*es['md_weeks'])/np.sum(w_random)
    se_random = np.sqrt(1/np.sum(w_random))
    ci_low = md_random - 1.96*se_random
    ci_high = md_random + 1.96*se_random
    I2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/Q*100) if Q>0 and len(es)>1 else 0

    print('\nRandom-effects pooled mean difference (smokers - nonsmokers, weeks):')
    print('MD = {:.2f} weeks (95% CI {:.2f} to {:.2f}), tau^2 = {:.4f}, I^2 = {:.1f}%'.format(md_random, ci_low, ci_high, tau2, I2))

    # Store
    es.to_csv('healing_time_differences_descriptive.csv', index=False)

    # Plot
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4))
    y = np.arange(len(es))
    ax.errorbar(es['md_weeks'], y, xerr=1.96*es['se_md'], fmt='s', color='black')
    ax.axvline(0, color='grey', linestyle='--')
    ax.set_yticks(y)
    ax.set_yticklabels(es['id'])
    ax.set_xlabel('Mean difference in healing time (weeks), smokers - nonsmokers')
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    plt.tight_layout()
    fname = 'healing_time_diff_bar.png'
    plt.savefig(fname, dpi=300)
    print('Saved', fname)
"}

messages.content:
Here’s what the time‑to‑union data show, and how solid they are.

---

## 1. What data we actually have for healing time

From all the long‑bone papers, **only two strata** have enough information (mean, N, and variance) to do a conventional mean‑difference meta‑analysis:

1. **c6c5269e19 – Delayed Fracture Healing in Alcohol Abusers**  
   - Mixed long‑bone fractures: femur (intertrochanteric, subtrochanteric, periprosthetic) and tibia shaft.  
   - Healing time defined clinically: time from surgery to full painless weight bearing.  
   - Reported (smoking contrast only):
     - Smokers: 21 patients, **15.8 ± 2.9 weeks (SE)** → SD ≈ 13.3 weeks  
     - Nonsmokers: 9 patients, **18.2 ± 5.9 weeks (SE)** → SD ≈ 17.7 weeks  
   - Mean difference (smokers − nonsmokers) ≈ **−2.4 weeks** (smokers slightly faster), but with very large SDs and tiny N → extremely imprecise.

2. **da73e6f003 – Tibial shaft fractures with circular external fixator**  
   - Extra‑articular tibial shaft fractures.  
   - Healing defined radiographically (bridging callus on ≥3 cortices) → radiographic union.  
   - Reported:
     - Smokers: 13 patients, **27.54 ± 11.07 weeks**  
     - Nonsmokers: 19 patients, **21.37 ± 5.08 weeks**  
   - Mean difference (smokers − nonsmokers) ≈ **+6.17 weeks** (smokers slower).

Everything else either:

- Only has **median and range/IQR** without SDs, or  
- Reports time‑to‑union via hazard ratios or Kaplan–Meier curves without group means/SDs.

So for pooled MD, we’re limited to **just these two**.

---

## 2. Pooled mean difference (smokers − nonsmokers)

Random‑effects meta‑analysis on those two strata (all converted to weeks):

- **Askew 2011 (alcohol study)**: MD ≈ −2.4 weeks (huge SE ≈ 6.57)  
- **Alemdaroğlu 2009 (tibial shaft, circular fixator)**: MD ≈ +6.17 weeks (SE ≈ 3.28)

### Pooled result (random-effects, DerSimonian–Laird)

- **Pooled MD = +3.78 weeks**  
- 95% CI: **−3.76 to +11.31 weeks**  
- τ² ≈ 9.72 (substantial between‑study variance for just 2 studies)  
- I² ≈ **26.5%**

Interpretation:

> With only two small, heterogeneous strata, the pooled estimate suggests **smokers may heal ~4 weeks slower on average**, but the confidence interval is very wide and includes **no difference at all**. Statistically this is **non‑significant and very unstable**.

The plot `healing_time_diff_bar.png` just visualizes those two MDs with CIs.

---

## 3. How this fits with the rest of the picture

- The **original LEAP open‑tibia study** and several others report **clearly longer healing times in smokers** (e.g., Schmitz tibial shaft 269 vs 136 days, LEAP time‑to‑union differences), but they do so via:
  - Medians and ranges, not means/SDs, or  
  - **Hazard ratios** from Cox models (time‑to‑event analyses).
- Our current MD pooling is conservative because we **did not impute SDs from medians/ranges** (which can be done but adds assumptions), nor did we integrate HRs into a separate time‑to‑event meta‑analysis.

So:

- The **nonunion crude OR meta‑analysis** clearly shows increased risk in smokers (OR ≈ 2.4).  
- The **infection crude ORs** show at most a very weak, non‑significant trend for superficial infection and essentially no deep infection signal.  
- The **time‑to‑union MD meta‑analysis** is underpowered and inconclusive as currently implemented, even though individual larger studies (not fully poolable here) report clearly longer healing times for smokers.

---

## 4. Options for strengthening the healing‑time analysis

If you want a more informative healing‑time synthesis, there are two technically heavier options:

1. **Convert medians + ranges/IQRs to approximate means + SDs**  
   - Use standard formulas (e.g., Wan/Hozo methods) to approximate means and SDs from medians, quartiles, and ranges.  
   - This would let us include:
     - Schmitz 1999 tibial shaft (269 vs 136 days).  
     - Ristiniemi distal tibia (medians and IQRs).  
   - Caveat: introduces approximation error; we’d explicitly flag which studies are “imputed.”

2. **Time‑to‑event meta-analysis using hazard ratios**  
   - For studies like LEAP that report **HRs for time to union** in smokers vs nonsmokers, we can meta‑analyze HRs instead of MDs.  
   - That’s closer to the original paper’s survival‑analysis approach.

Either of those would move us closer to the original review’s handling of time‑to‑union.

---

## 5. Where to go next

Given where we are, you have a few choices:

- **Stop here for time‑to‑union** and rely on:
  - Strong nonunion effect,  
  - Weak/no infection effect,  
  - Qualitative statement that time‑to‑union appears longer in smokers in several key studies, but our strict MD pooling is underpowered.

- Or, let me:
  1) **Impute means/SDs from medians/ranges** where needed and rerun a broader MD meta‑analysis; and/or  
  2) Build a **time‑to‑event (HR) meta‑analysis** for healing time in the subset of studies that report HRs.

If you tell me which of those you prefer (imputed MDs, HRs, or both), I’ll set up the next round of analysis that way.
Working on median-to-mean imputation for healing time; first I'll inspect the time-to-union dataset for available medians and ranges.

## 1. Strata with usable mean + variance

From all the long‑bone studies, only **two** strata have enough numeric detail (N, mean, and an SD or SE) to support a standard mean‑difference (MD) meta‑analysis:

1. **Askew 2011 – Alcohol abusers (c6c5269e19)**  
   - Fracture sites: femur (intertrochanteric, subtrochanteric, periprosthetic) and tibia shaft.  
   - Healing definition: clinical – time from operation to **full painless weight bearing**.  
   - Smoking contrast: smokers vs nonsmokers.
   - Reported:
     - Smokers: n = 21, 15.8 ± 2.9 weeks (SE) → SD ≈ 13.3 weeks  
     - Nonsmokers: n = 9, 18.2 ± 5.9 weeks (SE) → SD ≈ 17.7 weeks  
   - Mean difference (smokers – nonsmokers): **−2.40 weeks**, SE ≈ 6.57 (very imprecise).

2. **Alemdaroğlu 2009 – Tibial shaft, circular external fixator (da73e6f003)**  
   - Fracture site: extra‑articular tibial shaft fractures.  
   - Healing definition: radiographic – bridging callus on ≥3 cortices (AP + lateral).  
   - Smoking contrast: smokers vs non‑smokers.
   - Reported:
     - Smokers: n = 13, 27.54 ± 11.07 weeks  
     - Nonsmokers: n = 19, 21.37 ± 5.08 weeks  
   - Mean difference (smokers – nonsmokers): **+6.17 weeks**, SE ≈ 3.28.

These are the only strata where the analyst captured enough information for a standard MD with variance.

---

## 2. Attempt to use medians (option 1)

We then inspected the `TimeToUnionBySmoking` file for **median‑only** rows (`no_mean_sd_value == True`):

- Only **one** row is flagged: **c0e963edee – Nonunion of the femoral diaphysis**.  
- For **Schmitz 1999** (tibial shaft, 269 vs ~136 days), the analyst did capture medians and Ns, but not min/max or quartiles in structured fields, so we *don’t* have enough to apply standard median→mean SD formulas without going back to the PDFs.

Critically:

- We **do not** currently have, in structured form, the min/max or IQR needed to do proper Hozo/Wan‑type mean/SD imputation by smoking group.
- For Ristiniemi 2007 (distal tibia), we have a **single overall median (20 weeks, IQR 17–30)**, but **no separate medians for smokers vs nonsmokers**, so it can’t yield a group MD.

So with the data as extracted, “option 1” doesn’t yet add any additional usable strata beyond the two above. To genuinely expand the time‑to‑union dataset via median→mean imputation we’d need to:

- Re‑extract, for specific studies (e.g. Schmitz 1999, Ristiniemi 2007, LEAP if applicable), the **group‑specific medians plus ranges or quartiles**, then apply the formulas.

---

## 3. Pooled mean difference (with current data)

Using just the two strata with full mean/variance information:

- **Askew 2011 (alcohol)**: MD ≈ −2.40 weeks (smokers a bit faster; extremely noisy).  
- **Alemdaroğlu 2009 (tibial shaft, circular EF)**: MD ≈ +6.17 weeks (smokers slower).

### Random-effects meta-analysis (smokers – nonsmokers, weeks)

- **Pooled MD = +3.78 weeks**  
- 95% CI: **−3.76 to +11.31 weeks**  
- τ² ≈ 9.72, **I² ≈ 26.5%** (some heterogeneity, but only 2 studies).

Interpretation:

> With only two small, quite different strata, the pooled estimate is **inconclusive**: it suggests smokers might heal about **4 weeks slower**, but the confidence interval is wide and easily includes **no real difference** (and even slightly faster healing in smokers, as in the alcohol study).

The figure `healing_time_diff_bar.png` just visualizes these two study‑level MDs and their CIs.

---

## 4. Bottom line on healing time (given current extraction)

- Multiple primary papers (especially Schmitz 1999, LEAP, Adams 2001, etc.) **qualitatively report longer healing times in smokers**, sometimes very clearly.
- Our **nonunion analysis** already shows a robust effect (OR ≈ 2.4).  
- However, with the numeric fields we currently have, the time‑to‑union meta‑analysis is **data‑limited** and doesn’t add a strong, independent quantitative signal.

To push further on **option 1** in a robust way, we’d need to:

- Direct an analyst to go back to 2–3 key studies (e.g. Schmitz 1999, Ristiniemi 2007, LEAP) specifically to extract, by smoking group:
  - medians,  
  - quartiles or ranges,  
  - Ns,
- Then I could apply the standard median→mean/SD conversions and rerun the MD meta‑analysis with more than two data points.

If you want, I can set up that **targeted re‑extraction** step next for those specific studies, with the clear goal: “pull medians + IQR or ranges by smoking group for healing time.” Otherwise, we can treat the time‑to‑union evidence as primarily **qualitative** and move on to summarizing the full picture (nonunion + infection + time) and/or doing LOE/quality‑based sensitivity analyses.
lets go for a broader re-extraction that make sure we have what we need to for analysis
Working on that now...

{"name":"Time-to-Union Re-extraction Analyst","question":"We previously extracted time-to-union (healing time) stratified by smoking status, but for many key studies the variance estimates (SD/SE) or full distributional summaries (medians, ranges, IQRs) were incomplete. Please perform a targeted re-extraction focused on time-to-union for the following long-bone fracture-healing studies ONLY:

[1e482c3c3a, 6d465f919c, c6c5269e19, da73e6f003, f3b3fb9a95, f7e1801e7a, f9f2375ade, 920dc3d62b]

Scoping constraints:
- Do NOT include ankle-only or hip-only time-to-union data (e.g., 3b3475937c, 620fb1773e, 6dfe436834, 9ac67a783a); these are reserved for infection-only analyses in this project.
- Do NOT attempt time-to-union extraction for nonunion-only risk factor papers where healing time is not stratified by smoking (e.g., a154656aa1, bc42862567, c0e963edee), unless you find explicit smoker vs nonsmoker healing-time summaries.

For EACH of the listed papers, and for EVERY clearly defined stratum where time-to-union is reported by smoking/tobacco status (or the closest contrast), re-extract the following in a way that is as complete as possible for meta-analysis:

1) Study and stratum descriptors:
- Study ID and full citation (authors, year, journal if available).
- Fracture site(s): tibial shaft, distal tibia, femoral shaft, multiple long bones, or other long-bone description.
- Fracture type: open only, closed only, or mixed; include Gustilo grade ranges if time-to-union is presented by grade.
- Stratum descriptor: e.g., "all fractures", "tibial shaft only", "open tibial fractures only", or other clearly defined subgroups.

2) Smoking exposure and comparison:
- Exact smoking/tobacco categories used in the healing-time analysis (e.g., current vs never, current+former vs never, smokers vs nonsmokers, heavy vs non-heavy).
- Clarify the comparison used for time-to-union (e.g., current vs never; current+former vs never; heavy vs non-heavy). If multiple contrasts are presented, prefer the one closest to "current (or ever) smokers vs never smokers" and note the choice.

3) Union / healing-time definition and follow-up:
- Definition of "union" or "healing" used for the time-to-union metric (e.g., full painless weight bearing + bridging of ≥3 cortices; radiographic criteria only; clinical criteria only; composite definition).
- Whether healing time is measured on a clinical, radiographic, or combined basis.
- Minimum follow-up duration relevant to the healing-time assessment.

4) FULL distributional healing-time data by smoking status (per stratum):
For each smoking/tobacco group included in the selected comparison, please extract **all available summary statistics**, not just a single number:
- Group label (e.g., current smoker, previous smoker, combined smoker group, never smoker, heavy smoker, etc.).
- Number of patients in that group contributing to the healing-time analysis.
- **Mean time to union**, with its unit (weeks, days, or months).
- **Standard deviation (SD)** of time to union for that group, if reported.
- If only **standard error (SE)** is reported, extract SE and N so SD can be derived.
- If **means are not reported**, but **medians** are, extract:
  * Median time to union.
  * Minimum and maximum, if reported.
  * First and third quartiles (Q1, Q3) or interquartile range (IQR), if reported.
  * Any other distributional descriptors (e.g., percentiles) that may be available.
- Record the original units (days, weeks, months) exactly as stated.

5) Time-to-event effect measures if present:
- If the study reports only **time-to-event effect measures** for union/healing by smoking status (e.g., hazard ratios from Cox models), extract:
  * Effect measure type (e.g., hazard ratio for time to fracture healing comparing smokers vs nonsmokers) and its 95% confidence interval.
  * Model type (e.g., Cox proportional hazards), covariates adjusted for, and any notes on censoring patterns.
  * Make it clear that no group-level mean/SD or median/IQR is available in that case.

The goal is to build a more complete dataset of healing-time distributions by smoking status that includes means+SDs where possible and medians+IQR/ranges where not, across these long-bone fracture-healing studies. This will allow us to (a) run a standard mean-difference meta-analysis on the studies with means/SDs, and (b) optionally approximate means/SDs from medians and ranges/IQRs where needed. Please ensure that **all** distributional statistics that are present in the papers are captured, even if redundant, rather than only a single central tendency value.","require_file_output":true}

messages.content:
Response from Time-to-Union Re-extraction Analyst: Below is a structured summary of the re‑extracted healing‑time information by smoking status for the eight specified long‑bone fracture‑healing studies. I focus only on long‑bone (mostly tibial) fractures and on strata where time to union/healing is related to smoking. Where the paper did not provide usable healing‑time distributions, I state this explicitly. For meta‑analysis, you will generally have: - Means and SDs: Askew 2011 (alcohol/smoking), circular external fixator tibial shaft study, Adams 2001; plus partial (means only) for the tibial‑shaft outcome study and the clinical/occupational tibial shaft series. - Medians only: classic tibial‑shaft fracture healing paper. - Time‑to‑event model coefficients only: LEAP open tibia; distal tibia two‑ring hybrid Ilizarov. --- 1) LEAP limb‑threatening open tibia fractures – 1e482c3c3a Study & strata - Citation: “Impact of Smoking on Fracture Healing and Risk of Complications in Limb‑Threatening Open Tibia Fractures” (LEAP study cohort; journal details not fully captured in extraction). - Fracture site: unilateral open tibia fractures (long‑bone; no ankle/hip data). - Fracture type: open tibial fractures across Gustilo‑Anderson grades (III and below); analysis focuses on reconstructive pathway patients. - Stratum: all unilateral open tibia fractures in the LEAP reconstructive‑treatment cohort. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories for fracture‑healing analyses: never smoked, previous smoker, current smoker; defined from lifetime ≥100 cigarettes and current smoking status. - Primary contrast for healing time: current smokers vs nonsmokers (never + former) in Cox time‑to‑healing models. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: combined clinical and radiographic – “fracture healing was defined using both radiographic union (bridging of the fracture site) and clinical assessment, specifically when the patient is able to bear weight and perform activities and experiences no pain at the fracture site.” - Basis: composite clinical + radiographic. - Follow‑up: individuals not healed by 2 years were censored; time‑to‑union modeled up to 2‑year follow‑up. Distributional healing‑time data - The paper reports survival curves and Cox models; no group‑level mean/SD or median/IQR time‑to‑union stratified by smoking was found in the extracted content. Time‑to‑event effect measure - Effect type: hazard ratio (HR) for time to fracture healing comparing current smokers vs nonsmokers. - Value (adjusted): HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.44–0.90; p = 0.01. - Interpretation: current smokers were 37% less likely to be healed at any time point than nonsmokers (slower time to union). - Model: Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for: - bone loss > 2 cm, - Injury Severity Score (ISS) > 13, - moderate to severe muscle injury (AO Muscle/Tendon > 2), - low social support, - Gustilo tibia fracture grade > IIIA, - < high school education, - requirement for fracture‑stimulating surgery. - Note: Only time‑to‑event HRs and curves: no extractable mean/SD or median/IQR by smoking group. --- 2) Tibial shaft fractures – “Effect of Smoking on Tibial Shaft Fracture Healing” – 6d465f919c Study & strata - Citation: “Effect of Smoking on Tibial Shaft Fracture Healing” (journal/year not captured in the brief extraction, but consistent with a classic tibial‑shaft study). - Fracture site: tibial shaft fractures. - Fracture type: closed and Gustilo grade I open tibial shaft fractures. - Main stratum for smoking comparison: all treatment groups combined (intramedullary nail, external fixation, cast immobilization) for time to clinical union. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: smokers vs nonsmokers. - Smoking definition: smoking >5 cigarettes/day counted as smoking; ≤5 cigarettes/day and passive smoking counted as nonsmoking. Patients who quit before or within 1 week of treatment were classified as nonsmokers. - Primary contrast: smokers vs nonsmokers. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: purely clinical. - Clinical union: ability to ambulate and bear full weight on the affected tibia without pain at the fracture site and lack of pain or motion with manual three‑point stressing in sagittal and coronal planes. - Basis: clinical only. - Follow‑up: fractures followed “to union or beyond 1 year”; 44 of 76 tibias in smokers and 59 of 70 tibias in nonsmokers had follow‑up to union or >1 year. Distributional healing‑time data by smoking status - Smokers: - Group label: smokers. - N (healing‑time analysis): 44 tibias with follow‑up to union or >1 year. - Median time to clinical healing: 269 days. - Unit: days. - No mean, SD, SE, min, max, or quartiles were reported in the extracted text. - Nonsmokers: - N: 59 tibias. - Median time to clinical healing: 136 days. - Unit: days. Time‑to‑event / survival - The primary reported contrast is the difference in median time to union; survival‑type curves are shown but no HRs or regression coefficients are provided in the extracted content. --- 3) Alcohol and smoking in fracture healing – Askew et al. – c6c5269e19 Study & strata - Citation (assembled): Askew et al. 2011. “Delayed Fracture Healing in Alcohol Abusers—A Preliminary Retrospective Study.” The Open Bone Journal. - Fracture sites: intertrochanteric femur, subtrochanteric femur, periprosthetic femur, and tibial shaft fractures (long bones only). - Fracture type: mixed long‑bone fracture types: - 20 intertrochanteric (7 alcoholics, 13 nonalcoholics), - 6 tibia shaft (3 alcoholics, 3 nonalcoholics), - 2 subtrochanteric, 2 periprosthetic. - Relevant stratum for smoking: “all smokers (alcoholics and nonalcoholics) as a group” vs all nonsmokers across the long‑bone set. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: smokers vs nonsmokers, pooled across alcohol status. - Smoking definition: any documented “history of smoking” in the chart. - Primary contrast for healing time: all smokers (alcoholic + nonalcoholic) vs all nonsmokers. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: clinical. - “Fracture healing time was defined as the period of time from the operative treatment of the fracture to the time at which full painless weight bearing was resumed.” - Basis: clinical time to full painless weight bearing. - Follow‑up: not explicitly time‑limited in the extraction; standard post‑operative clinical follow‑up until full painless weight bearing. Distributional healing‑time data by smoking status - Smokers (all smokers, alcoholics and nonalcoholics): - Group label: smokers. - N: 9 patients. - Mean time to union: 18.2 weeks. - SD vs SE: The abstract specifies that fracture healing time is reported as “mean ± standard error.” The value “± 5.9 weeks” for smokers is therefore SE. - SE of time to union: 5.9 weeks. - SD: can be derived later as SD = SE × √N ≈ 5.9 × √9 = 17.7 weeks (not computed in the extraction but derivable from N and SE). - Units: weeks. - No median, min, max, or quartiles are given. - Nonsmokers (all nonsmokers): - N: 21 patients. - Reported mean ± SE (from abstract): 15.8 ± 2.9 weeks; N = 21 (for comparison with smokers). These values apply to the long‑bone cohort as a whole. --- 4) Circular external fixator for tibial shaft fractures – da73e6f003 Study & strata - Citation: “Factors affecting the fracture healing in treatment of tibial shaft fractures with circular external fixator.” - Fracture site: extraarticular tibial shaft fractures. - Fracture type: mixed open and closed fractures. - Table 2 reports mean consolidation time by open vs closed, confirming mixed fracture type. - Stratum: all extraarticular tibial shaft fractures treated with circular external fixator. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: smokers vs non‑smokers. - In Table 2, the “Smoking” variable is coded as Yes vs No. - Primary contrast: Yes (smokers) vs No (non‑smokers), as part of a univariate comparison of mean consolidation time. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: radiographic. - “The time for consolidation was defined when there was bridging callus between the main fragments on at least three cortices on A–P and lateral X‑rays, which was obviously denser than the opacity of the medullar canal of the intact bone.” - Basis: purely radiographic. - Follow‑up: “The patients were followed monthly clinically and radiographically for at least 6 months after union.” Distributional healing‑time data by smoking status (consolidation time) - Smokers (Smoking = Yes): - Group label: smokers. - N: 13 fractures. - Mean consolidation time: 27.54 weeks. - SD: 11.069 weeks (reported as mean ± SD). - Units: weeks. - No median, range, or quartiles were provided. - Non‑smokers (Smoking = No): - N: 19 fractures. - Mean consolidation time: 21.37 weeks. - SD: 5.079 weeks. - Units: weeks. No separate time‑to‑event model or hazard ratio was reported for smoking in the extracted content; the comparison is via univariate means and p‑value (p = 0.107 for smokers vs non‑smokers). --- 5) Cigarette smoking and tibial shaft outcome – f3b3fb9a95 Study & strata - Citation: “Cigarette smoking influences the clinical and occupational outcome of patients with tibial shaft fractures.” - Fracture site: tibial shaft fractures. - Fracture type: mixed open and closed tibial shaft fractures. - Example from Table 1: open fractures 22.3% overall; distribution similar in smokers and nonsmokers. - Stratum: all tibial shaft fractures included in the clinical and occupational outcome analysis. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: group 1 (G1) never smokers; group 2 (G2) current and previous smokers. - Primary contrast: current + previous smokers vs never smokers. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition (termed “physiological fracture healing”): - full, pain‑free weight bearing within 4 months, - plus radiologic bridging of at least three cortices on AP and lateral radiographs. - Basis: composite clinical + radiographic. - Follow‑up: clinical and radiographic follow‑up until healing; not given as a fixed minimum, but healing within ~4 months was considered physiological. Distributional healing‑time data by smoking status (Table 4 – “Weeks until fracture healing**”) - Nonsmokers (G1): - Group label: never smoker. - N: 39 patients. - Mean weeks until fracture healing: 11.9 weeks. - Median: 11 weeks. - Range: 8–32 weeks. - Units: weeks. - Current and previous smokers (G2): - N: 46 patients. - Mean weeks until fracture healing: 17.4 weeks. - Median: 14 weeks. - Range: 8–63 weeks. - Units: weeks. - Total (all patients): - N: 85. - Mean: 14.9 weeks. - Median: 12 weeks. - Range: 8–63 weeks. The table uses the format “mean (median; min–max)” – no SD or SE is provided, and no quartiles or IQR are reported. --- 6) Two‑ring hybrid Ilizarov for distal tibia fractures – f7e1801e7a Study & strata - Citation: “Two‑ring Hybrid External Fixation of Distal Tibial Fractures: A Review of 47 Cases.” - Fracture site: distal tibial fractures (long bone; not ankle‑only – fixation is for distal tibial metaphyseal region). - Fracture type: AO/OTA A and C types, including intra‑ and extra‑articular distal tibial fractures. - Stratum: all distal tibial fractures treated with two‑ring hybrid external fixation. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: current smokers vs nonsmokers (smoking status used as a risk factor in regression for delayed union/time to union). - Primary contrast: current smoking vs not current smoking. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: combined radiographic and clinical. - “Fractures were considered united when AP and lateral radiographs showed bridging of three out of four cortices or the fracture lines had disappeared and there was no pain in the fracture upon weight bearing.” - Basis: clinical + radiographic. - Follow‑up: clinical and radiographic follow‑up until union; length not fixed, but delays in union analyzed. Distributional healing‑time data - No explicit group‑level mean/SD or median/IQR times to union stratified by smoking were found in the extracted content. Time‑to‑event / regression effect measure - Effect type: linear regression coefficient for delay in time to union attributable to smoking. - Reported value: Smoking “delayed fracture union by 10 weeks (regression coefficient 10.1, 95% CI: –1.21; p = 0.070).” - Effect measure: β = 10.1 weeks (increase in time to union for current smokers vs nonsmokers). - 95% CI (as reported): approximately –1.2 to +21.4 weeks (only the lower bound is quoted directly; upper bound not fully captured in the extraction, but the text indicates a CI spanning –1.21 with p = 0.070). - Model description: multivariable linear regression with time to union as the outcome; current smoking included among risk factors along with fracture displacement and other variables. - Note: This is not a Cox model; there are no HRs, and no distributional summaries (mean/SD by group) are reported in the extracted text. --- 7) Open tibia fractures – Adams et al. 2001 – f9f2375ade Study & strata - Citation: Adams CL et al. 2001. Injury, International Journal of the Care of the Injured, 32:61–65. - Fracture site: open tibial fractures (long‑bone; tibia only). - Fracture type: open fractures (Gustilo grades analyzed; full range I–III). - Stratum: all open tibial fractures combined. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: regular smokers vs nonsmokers. - Smoking defined as ≥10 cigarettes/day. - Non‑smokers defined by documentation as non‑smokers in the chart. - Primary contrast: smokers vs nonsmokers. Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: composite clinical and radiographic. - “A fracture was deemed to be united when the patient could fully weight bear with no pain at the fracture site and there was radiographic evidence of bridging of three of the four cortices on standard AP and lateral views.” - Basis: clinical + radiographic. - Follow‑up: not stated as a single minimum, but patients followed until union or nonunion determination; union and nonunion rates assessed over course of treatment. Distributional healing‑time data by smoking status - Smokers (Group I): - Group label: smokers. - N (healing‑time analysis): 140 patients (derived as total fractures in group I: 65 nail + 50 external fixation + 25 plaster). - Mean time to union: 32.3 weeks. - Unit: weeks. - Variance estimates (SD/SE) are not reported in the extracted text; Table 4 provides mean times and p‑values only. - Nonsmokers (Group II): - N: 133 patients. - Mean time to union: 27.8 weeks. - Unit: weeks. - No SD/SE, medians, or quartiles provided in the extracted content. Time‑to‑event measures - Not reported; analysis is based on group mean times and complication rates, not hazard ratios. --- 8) Open tibia fractures, debriedment timing – “Open Tibia Fractures: Timely Debridement Leaves Injury Severity as the Only Determinant of Poor Outcome” – 920dc3d62b Study & strata - Citation: “Open Tibia Fractures: Timely Debridement Leaves Injury Severity as the Only Determinant of Poor Outcome.” - Fracture site: open tibia shaft fractures (OTA 42 A–C). - Fracture type: open fractures graded I–IIIc by Gustilo–Anderson. - Stratum: all open tibia shaft fractures in the 36‑month prospective series. Smoking exposure & contrast - Categories: smokers vs nonsmokers (smoking appears as a baseline characteristic; used in risk models for nonunion but not for time‑to‑union distributions). Union definition & follow‑up - Union definition: radiologic and clinical, based on RUST scoring: - Patients with RUST 10–12 without pain and tenderness were classified as united (radiologic and clinical union). - Basis: composite clinical + radiographic. - Follow‑up: 12‑month follow‑up reported for the cohort. Distributional healing‑time data & effect measures - The paper reports union rates and logistic regression odds ratios for nonunion at 12 months (including smoking), but there is no group‑level summary of time to union stratified by smoking in the extracted content. - N in smoking group at 12 months: derived as 13 united + 10 nonunion smokers = 23 smokers at 12 months (from Table 2), but no time‑to‑union distribution is given. - Note explicitly: For this study, no usable mean/SD or median/IQR of time to union by smoking status is available; only union/nonunion status at 6 and 12 months and adjusted ORs for nonunion. --- Studies where time‑to‑union by smoking was not fully available - LEAP open tibia (1e482c3c3a): provides a Cox HR for time to union (current smokers vs nonsmokers) but no group‑level mean/SD or median/IQR times to union. - Distal tibia hybrid Ilizarov (f7e1801e7a): reports a regression coefficient indicating roughly 10‑week delay for current smokers, but no separate mean/SD or median/IQR distributions by smoking. - Debridement/open tibia outcome (920dc3d62b): provides union/nonunion proportions and logistic regression for nonunion; no time‑to‑union summary by smoking. --- Meta‑analytic usability summary 1) Studies with mean and SD (or SE + N allowing SD derivation) by smoking group: - Askew et al. 2011 (c6c5269e19): all long‑bone smokers vs nonsmokers. - Smokers: mean 18.2 weeks, SE 5.9, N=9 (SD can be derived). - Nonsmokers: mean 15.8 weeks, SE 2.9, N=21 (SD can be derived). - Circular external fixator tibial shaft (da73e6f003): smokers vs non‑smokers. - Smokers: mean 27.54 weeks, SD 11.07, N=13. - Non‑smokers: mean 21.37 weeks, SD 5.08, N=19. 2) Studies with mean but no variance (potential use if approximate SDs are input via external methods or meta‑analysis of means only): - Cigarette smoking and tibial shaft outcome (f3b3fb9a95): - Nonsmokers: mean 11.9 weeks, median 11, range 8–32, N=39. - Smokers (current + previous): mean 17.4 weeks, median 14, range 8–63, N=46. - You can use the medians and ranges with standard conversion formulae to approximate SDs. - Adams open tibia fractures (f9f2375ade): - Smokers: mean 32.3 weeks, N=140. - Nonsmokers: mean 27.8 weeks, N=133. - No variance; may require imputation from similar studies or external assumptions. 3) Studies with medians only: - Classic tibial shaft healing (6d465f919c): - Smokers: median 269 days, N=44. - Nonsmokers: median 136 days, N=59. - Survival curves (if digitized externally) could be used to approximate means/SDs, but not available in this extraction. 4) Studies with time‑to‑event regression only: - LEAP open tibia (1e482c3c3a): HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.44–0.90), current vs non‑smokers. - Distal tibia hybrid Ilizarov (f7e1801e7a): regression coefficient +10.1 weeks delay (95% CI approximately –1.2 to +21), current smokers vs nonsmokers. - Debridement timing in open tibia (920dc3d62b): logistic regression ORs for nonunion; no healing‑time distributions. These re‑extractions now provide, for the targeted long‑bone studies you specified, the most complete set of healing‑time distributions and time‑to‑event estimates stratified by smoking status that can be obtained from the available text. They should support (a) a standard mean‑difference meta‑analysis in the subset with means/SDs or convertible SEs, and (b) approximate mean/SD reconstruction from median + range/IQR where only those are reported. **Data collections attached**: TimeToUnionBySmoking_LongBone_8Papers
Evidence provided by Time-to-Union Re-extraction Analyst: Key extracted data points by study and smoking group: 1) LEAP open tibia – 1e482c3c3a - Union definition: “Fracture healing was defined using both radiographic union (bridging of the fracture site) and clinical assessment, specifically when the patient is able to bear weight and perform activities and experiences no pain at the fracture site.” - Smoking categories: “For this analysis, the study group was divided into 3 smoking categories: never smoked (n = 81), previous smoker (n = 82), and current smoker (n = 105).” - Time‑to‑event effect: current smokers vs nonsmokers – “Current smoker | 0.630 (0.90–0.44) | 0.01” (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.44–0.90). 2) Tibial shaft clinical union – 6d465f919c - Union definition: “Clinical union was defined as the ability of the patient to ambulate and bear full weight on the affected tibia without pain at the fracture site and lack of pain or motion at the fracture site with manual three-point stressing of the fracture in the sagittal and coronal planes.” - Smoking definition: “Smoking five or fewer cigarettes per day and passive smoking were not considered smoking for the purposes of the study. {"code":"import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Manually construct healing-time dataset for MD meta-analysis
# All units in weeks; smokers - nonsmokers

rows = []

# 1) Askew 2011 (c6c5269e19) - long-bone fractures, smokers vs nonsmokers
# From abstract: smokers n=21, 15.8 ± 2.9 weeks (SE); nonsmokers n=9, 18.2 ± 5.9 weeks (SE)
N_smokers = 21
N_nonsmokers = 9
mean_s = 15.8
mean_ns = 18.2
SE_s = 2.9
SE_ns = 5.9
SD_s = SE_s * np.sqrt(N_smokers)
SD_ns = SE_ns * np.sqrt(N_nonsmokers)
rows.append({
    'id': 'c6c5269e19',
    'study': 'Askew 2011 (alcohol, mixed long-bone)',
    'N_smokers': N_smokers,
    'N_nonsmokers': N_nonsmokers,
    'mean_smokers_wk': mean_s,
    'mean_nonsmokers_wk': mean_ns,
    'sd_smokers_wk': SD_s,
    'sd_nonsmokers_wk': SD_ns
})

# 2) Alemdaroglu 2009 (da73e6f003) - tibial shaft, circular EF, smokers vs non-smokers
N_smokers = 13
N_nonsmokers = 19
mean_s = 27.54
mean_ns = 21.37
SD_s = 11.069
SD_ns = 5.079
rows.append({
    'id': 'da73e6f003',
    'study': 'Alemdaroglu 2009 (tibial shaft, circular EF)',
    'N_smokers': N_smokers,
    'N_nonsmokers': N_nonsmokers,
    'mean_smokers_wk': mean_s,
    'mean_nonsmokers_wk': mean_ns,
    'sd_smokers_wk': SD_s,
    'sd_nonsmokers_wk': SD_ns
})

# 3) Moghaddam 2011 (f3b3fb9a95) - tibial shaft, G1 vs G2, means + ranges, no SD
# Nonsmokers (G1): N=39, mean 11.9, median 11, range 8–32 weeks
# Smokers (G2): N=46, mean 17.4, median 14, range 8–63 weeks
# Approximate SD from range: SD ≈ (max - min)/4 for n between 15 and 70
N_smokers = 46
N_nonsmokers = 39
mean_s = 17.4
mean_ns = 11.9
range_s = 63 - 8
range_ns = 32 - 8
SD_s = range_s / 4.0
SD_ns = range_ns / 4.0
rows.append({
    'id': 'f3b3fb9a95',
    'study': 'Moghaddam 2011 (tibial shaft, clinical outcome)',
    'N_smokers': N_smokers,
    'N_nonsmokers': N_nonsmokers,
    'mean_smokers_wk': mean_s,
    'mean_nonsmokers_wk': mean_ns,
    'sd_smokers_wk': SD_s,
    'sd_nonsmokers_wk': SD_ns
})

es = pd.DataFrame(rows)

# Compute mean differences and SEs (smokers - nonsmokers)
es['md_wk'] = es['mean_smokers_wk'] - es['mean_nonsmokers_wk']
es['se_md'] = np.sqrt(es['sd_smokers_wk']**2/es['N_smokers'] + es['sd_nonsmokers_wk']**2/es['N_nonsmokers'])

print('Study-level MDs (weeks, smokers - nonsmokers):')
print(es[['id','study','md_wk','se_md']])

# Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird)
if len(es) > 0:
    w_fixed = 1/es['se_md']**2
    md_fixed = np.sum(w_fixed*es['md_wk'])/np.sum(w_fixed)
    Q = np.sum(w_fixed*(es['md_wk'] - md_fixed)**2)
    df_Q = len(es) - 1
    C = np.sum(w_fixed) - np.sum(w_fixed**2)/np.sum(w_fixed)
    tau2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/C) if len(es) > 1 else 0
    w_random = 1/(es['se_md']**2 + tau2)
    md_random = np.sum(w_random*es['md_wk'])/np.sum(w_random)
    se_random = np.sqrt(1/np.sum(w_random))
    ci_low = md_random - 1.96*se_random
    ci_high = md_random + 1.96*se_random
    I2 = max(0, (Q-df_Q)/Q*100) if Q>0 and len(es)>1 else 0

    print('\nRandom-effects pooled MD (weeks, smokers - nonsmokers):')
    print('MD = {:.2f} weeks (95% CI {:.2f} to {:.2f}), tau^2 = {:.4f}, I^2 = {:.1f}%'.format(md_random, ci_low, ci_high, tau2, I2))

    # Save
    es.to_csv('TimeToUnionSmoking_Complete.csv', index=False)

    # Forest-style plot (MDs)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4))
    y = np.arange(len(es))
    ax.errorbar(es['md_wk'], y, xerr=1.96*es['se_md'], fmt='s', color='black')
    # pooled summary
    idx_pool = len(es)
    ax.errorbar([md_random], [idx_pool], xerr=[1.96*se_random], fmt='s', color='red')
    labels = list(es['id']) + ['Pooled']
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(es)+1))
    ax.set_yticklabels(labels)
    ax.axvline(0, color='grey', linestyle='--')
    ax.set_xlabel('Mean difference in healing time (weeks), smokers - nonsmokers')
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    plt.tight_layout()
    fname = 'healing_time_diff_bar_imputed.png'
    plt.savefig(fname, dpi=300)
    print('Saved', fname)
"}
